title: No generic AsyncDialogAction component
decision: Do not build it. Ownership of open state (D36) and the form boundary (D37) make correctness come from structure rather than from a wrapper.
context: The original proposal suggested an AsyncDialogAction helper to absorb the pattern of waiting for an async handler before closing. Its natural implementation is await onClick() followed by close().

alternatives.option: AsyncDialogAction implemented as await onClick() then close()
alternatives.reason: It does not fix the bug. Neither handler rejects on failure: form.handleSubmit(onSubmit)() calls onInvalid and resolves normally when validation fails, and createGame catches its own error and resolves with undefined. A generic await-then-close closes the dialog anyway, one tick later, while suggesting the problem is solved.

alternatives.option: Have AsyncDialogAction read RHF's formState.isValid, or require every handler to throw
alternatives.reason: The first binds a form library into a dialog component; the second rewrites every caller's error handling, after which the helper has nothing left to do.

consequences: There is no shared component, so no layer of indirection to decode.
The correct shape is structural and visible: the form boundary wraps the footer, and a DialogClose around a submit button looks out of place.
Nothing enforces it. Whether a Design System rule or a lint rule should is a separate decision.
revisitTriggers: A third dialog needs to close only on success under a condition a form boundary cannot express.
A lint rule is adopted that forbids an onClick on a Button under DialogClose asChild.
